### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. basal cell nevus syndrome 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.793)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:9585)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9585) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP467); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP467) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002670); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP467) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple basal cell carcinomas (HP:0002797); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP467) —LEADS_TO→ Odontogenic keratocyst (HP:0011224); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP467) —LEADS_TO→ Palmar or plantar pits (HP:0011770). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 disrupt the normal regulation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway. This dysregulation leads to uncontrolled cell proliferation and development of various phenotypes associated with both Gorlin syndrome (basal cell carcinoma, odontogenic keratocyst) and basal cell nevus syndrome 1 (multiple basal cell carcinomas, palmar/plantar pits).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PTCH1 with a clear dominant-negative effect or gain-of-function mechanism in affected individuals would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs113113496)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving PTCH1 and the Hedgehog pathway opens avenues for targeted therapies, such as Hedgehog signaling inhibitors, for both Gorlin syndrome and basal cell nevus syndrome 1.

#### 2. basal cell carcinoma, susceptibility to, 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.708)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:9585)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9585) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167964); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167964) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002670); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167964) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple basal cell carcinomas (HP:0002710). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which drives the development of basal cell carcinomas in both Gorlin syndrome and susceptibility to basal cell carcinoma 1.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in PTCH1 exhibiting a complete absence of basal cell carcinoma development would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if common variants with a frequency >1% in gnomAD are identified as the primary cause for either disease, this would weaken the hypothesis. _(variant: HGMD:M:9585)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway with inhibitors like vismodegib has proven effective in treating basal cell carcinomas, highlighting the translational relevance of understanding the shared genetic basis of these conditions.

#### 3. congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787, Reactome:R-HSA-5632684, Reactome:R-HSA-5635838, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9575) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457); SMO (HGNC:10700) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal vertebral development (HP:0000385); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Hypothalamic hamartoma (HP:0011679); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 or SMO disrupt the Hedgehog signaling pathway. This aberrant signaling leads to various developmental phenotypes observed in both Klippel-Feil syndrome and congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome, including vertebral abnormalities, hypothalamic hamartomas, epilepsy, intellectual disability, short stature, and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PTCH1 or SMO with a consistent loss-of-function effect in individuals with Klippel-Feil syndrome (MONDO:0012562) and congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome (MONDO:0009436) that do not impact the Hedgehog signaling pathway. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in PTCH1 or SMO in the affected populations with a frequency above 0.01% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway could offer therapeutic strategies for both Klippel-Feil syndrome and congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome, potentially by modulating pathway activity to correct developmental defects.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PTCH1 and SMO do not lead to a shared downstream disruption of the Hedgehog signaling pathway in both disease contexts, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping causal pathways for each disease. _(variant: Presence of common pathogenic variants (AF > 0.01) in PTCH1 or SMO in the general population that do not segregate with either disease.)_
